claim_summary: PandaAI contributes market-regime state modeling, finance-specific LLM adaptation, constrained alpha search, trading procedures, and feedback-driven updates for quantitative decision support.

claim_evidence.quote: We propose market regime latent variable modeling and a dual-channel adaptation mechanism, compressing high-dimensional market dynamics factors into continuous latent states zt to achieve unified market perception for LLM’s symbolic reasoning and the numerical optimization of quantitative modules.

We construct a closed-loop update system covering the full lifecycle of quantitative finance, combining fast logical constraint induction and slow parameter adaptation to realize continuous adaptation of the model to non-stationary financial markets

modules.name: Market-regime state and numerical control adapters
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:no—the state transform and control scalars do not encode a task-family output objective, and the time-indexed regime representation can remain if a downstream objective changes. R3_2_GTS:yes—it compresses temporal market factors into a regime state used by downstream modules.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - state transform has no task-specific output criterion
R3_2_GTS:yes - compresses time-varying market data into regime state

evidence.quote: To retain numerical fidelity while reducing noise, a lightweight Autoencoder architecture is employed to obtain the low-dimensional zt that preserves the continuous dynamic properties of the market.

Numerical Adapter for Control (Channel 2): For modules requiring scalar inputs (Portfolio P and Execution E), a separate feature extraction network maps zt to specific control parameters (e.g., risk aversion λt , liquidity participation rate γt ).

modules.name: Market-regime soft-token adapter
modules.scope_reason: R2: the projection maps a continuous temporal market state into trainable soft tokens prepended to the LLM input, changing model-side representation and alignment.

evidence.quote: Symbolic Adapter for LLM (Channel 1): To make the continuous vector zt comprehensible to the LLM, we employ a projection MLP that maps zt into k learnable soft tokens. These tokens are prepended to the LLM’s input embedding sequence.

modules.name: Finance-specific CQ2 instruction and reasoning tuning
modules.scope_reason: R2: SFT and preference training update CQ2 so its financial responses and reasoning are conditioned on market context.

evidence.quote: A financial instruction dataset DSFT is constructed where each sample v is tagged with the originating market state zt from Module M. Each sample v contains three components (x, y, zt ), where x denotes the question and y corresponds to the answer.
Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning A reasoning trace dataset VSF T QA is constructed, where each sample is a triplet v = (x, c, y).

modules.name: Financially constrained alpha-factor tree search
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:yes—the search objective generates formulaic factors under financial constraints and evaluates them by backtest; changing task family would require redesigning the factor action space and its financial objective and verifier.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - factor search embeds financial decision objectives and constraints

evidence.quote: We implement an LLMguided Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) framework to navigate this sparse solution space.
A formulaic alpha factor f is a symbolic expression mapping market history to a cross-sectional signal vector st ∈ RN where N represents the number of products in the panel.

modules.name: Regime-conditioned portfolio optimization
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:yes—the solver chooses portfolio weights to trade off alpha returns and financial risk under portfolio constraints; a different task family would require a different action space, objective, and constraints.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - portfolio weights optimize a financial return-risk objective

modules.name: Regime-conditioned trade execution control
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:yes—the policy selects trading strategies to minimize implementation shortfall using portfolio weights and inferred liquidity; changing task family would require new trading actions and execution objective.

evidence.quote: Execution Control (E) To minimize implementation shortfall (IS), the execution policy πexec (a|wt , zt ) selects strategies (e.g., TWAP, VWAP) isomorphic to the inferred liquidity profile.

modules.name: Trading-feedback symbolic constraint induction
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:yes—the induced rules encode financial alpha behavior and are appended to the trading constraint set; changing task family would require redesigning those predicates and criteria.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - induced predicates encode trading-specific constraints

evidence.quote: Upon detecting statistically significant failure clusters in E, the system triggers symbolic induction. By contrastively prompting the LLM with failed samples (Sharpe < 0) against successful ones within regime zt , U extracts logical predicates
These insights are formalized as symbolic rules (e.g., IF Trend(zt ) > τ THEN Ban(Reversal)) and immediately appended to C.

modules.name: Experience-replay LoRA model adaptation
modules.scope_reason: R2: LoRA updates CQ2 parameters from successful temporal-workflow trajectories and profitable execution feedback, training the model policy used to generate factors.

evidence.quote: successful trajectories (verified CoT traces and profitable executions) are stored in an experience replay buffer. We periodically update θ via LoRA [8] with a 5% data replay ratio [18].
